title: Chase Sapphire Reserve launches highest-ever 150,000-point bonus. Here's how it compares to other cards
raw_text:
Terms apply to American Express benefits and offers. Visit americanexpress.com to learn more.
The Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees) is now offering its highest points-only welcome bonus to date — and with the same spending requirement as its previous offer.
This bonus is available online starting Thursday and in Chase branches beginning May 3. While the offer doesn't currently have an end date, these types of elevated bonuses typically don't last long.
CNBC Select goes over this newest Sapphire Reserve bonus and how it stacks up against other popular travel rewards credit cards.
The Chase Sapphire Reserve® is a standout premium credit card with plenty of luxury perks and statement credits to justify its annual fee.
- Access over 1,300 airport lounges worldwide with a complimentary Priority PassTM Select membership, plus every Chase Sapphire Lounge® by The Club with two guests.
- Up to $300 in annual travel credit each account anniversary year
- You can transfer rewards to all of Chase's travel partners including World of Hyatt, Southwest Rapid Rewards and many more
- Top-tier travel and shopping protections
- High annual fee
- Requires a high credit score

If you're planning a summer trip or simply looking to stockpile valuable Chase Ultimate Rewards® points, the Chase Sapphire Reserve could be a great asset.
As of Thursday, new Sapphire Reserve cardholders who apply online can earn 150,000 points after spending $6,000 within the first three months from account opening. The offer extends to those applying in branch on May 3.
Experts generally value Chase Ultimate Rewards® points at roughly 2 cents apiece toward airline transfer partner travel, and you can glean 2 cents per point (or more) with Chase's Points Boost feature. As such, this new 150,000-point bonus could be worth roughly $3,000 toward travel.
CNBC Select previously confirmed with a Chase representative that consumer Sapphire cards have shifted to a once-per-lifetime welcome bonus rule. So, if you've already earned a Chase Sapphire Reserve bonus, you won't be eligible for future ones.
Offers in this section are from affiliate partners and selected based on a combination of engagement, product relevance, compensation, and consistent availability.
The last public welcome offer was 125,000 points after spending $6,000 in purchases in the first three months from account opening (offer no longer available). With the bonus increasing to 150,000 points — and the spending requirement staying the same — this new offer is 20% more valuable.
Past offers for the Sapphire Reserve have been as low as 60,000 to 80,000 points, but since the card was overhauled in the summer of 2025, its welcome bonuses have typically been at least six figures.
This is the Reserve's highest-ever welcome offer (a 2025 bonus was similar in value but included a combination of points and Chase Travel promo credits), so it could be a great time to apply.
While this is one of the highest welcome bonuses available, it still makes sense to compare it with current offers from other cards.
American Express Platinum Card®
The American Express Platinum Card is unique in that it doesn't offer a fixed welcome bonus. Instead, new cardholders can earn as high as 175,000 Membership Rewards® points after spending $12,000 on their new Card within the first six months from account opening.
This means you may earn less than the advertised bonus; it'll vary from person to person. Amex will tell you what your welcome bonus is before you have to accept the card, so you can factor that in. The card also requires double the spending of the Sapphire Reserve to qualify for the bonus, which might simply be too high a cost for many people (on top of its $895 annual fee, see rates and fees).
The American Express Platinum Card® is a premium card loaded with annual statement credits, entertainment benefits, extensive airport lounge access, elite status perks and more. (Enrollment required for select benefits mentioned)

Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card
With the Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card, new cardholders can earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. While this is only half the amount of the Sapphire Reserve's bonus, it also requires $2,000 less spending.
The Chase card's bonus might technically offer better value, but if you're looking for lower spending requirements, the Venture X could be a better fit. Plus, the Venture X offers similar premium perks — from airport lounge access to travel statement credits — but for a lower $395 annual fee ($400 less than the Sapphire Reserve).
The Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card is a premium credit card with a myriad of benefits and a lower annual fee than other high-end cards with similar features.

Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card
If the last two annual fees are too daunting, you could consider the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees). Its annual fee is only $95, making it much more manageable.
With the Sapphire Preferred, new cardholders can earn 75,000 bonus points after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first three months. While this is a solid offer, the bonus isn't the main draw — rather, the affordable annual fee compared to the $795 fee charged by the Sapphire Reserve.
Plus, the card still gives you access to Chase's transfer partners, a suite of travel insurance protections and perks like a 10,000-point anniversary bonus.
The Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card packs a punch for a $95 annual fee card, offering annual travel credits, comprehensive travel protections and more.
